card: Bitcoin Core aborts FlushStateToDisk with an error immediately if flushing block or undo files fails. Previously, a block-file flush failure logged a warning and initiated shutdown, but still proceeded to write block-tree metadata, flush the coins database, and advance the last-flushed block marker. This could cause on-disk chainstate and downstream persistent indexes to record blocks as committed even when the underlying block data failed to flush to disk. The change resolves a validation TODO and adds a unit test verifying flush failure boundaries.
changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor test and comment adjustments; the core change remains the same.
evidence: Resolves an existing TODO in src/validation.cpp: 'TODO: Handle return error, or add detailed comment why it is safe to not return an error upon failure.'

PR description highlights that PR #34897 introduced m_last_flushed_block to prevent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate, which would be violated if the marker advances despite failed block file flushes.
problem: When FlushChainstateBlockFile() fails, FlushStateToDisk() previously logged a warning and continued executing anyway. It wrote block-tree metadata, flushed the coins cache to disk, and advanced m_last_flushed_block, leaving on-disk chainstate and persistent indexes pointing to blocks whose underlying block data was never durably written to disk.

risk.why: Altering error handling in Chainstate::FlushStateToDisk() affects block connection and shutdown; a logic bug could trigger spurious flush aborts and prevent chainstate persistence.

summary: Aborts Chainstate::FlushStateToDisk() with an error if flushing block or undo files to disk fails. This prevents writing block-tree metadata and coins database records and keeps m_last_flushed_block at the last successful flush when block data could not be made durable. A unit test is added to verify that flush markers and coins DB state do not advance on failure.
